name: Roux and stock base
summary: A pair of kitchen bases: a stock made from bones and meat, and a roux of flour and butter that thickens it. Most French sauces of later styles begin here.
how: Simmer bones, meat and vegetables in water for several hours and strain the stock.
Cook flour in butter over low heat to the colour that the sauce needs.
Whisk the stock into the roux and simmer the sauce until it coats a spoon.

origin.note: La Varenne printed the roux as a sauce base in place of bread crumbs, and the stock as the base of a sauce and a soup.

adoptions.via: Carême built his grand sauces on stocks and a roux.
Escoffier kept the roux and the stock in the system of the hotel kitchen.
The restaurants of the provinces kept the classic stock and roux sauces.
